copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Saturday, evening UTC kickoff, brings Qatar and Switzerland together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Qatar side, by +11.8pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

Elo numbers going in: Qatar 1640, Switzerland 1830. That's a 190-point lead for Switzerland — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Qatar to win at 20%, the draw at 19%, and Switzerland to win at 61%. The Desk publishes a three-way read against the same W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on — not a scoreline guess. Qatar sits at 20% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Qatar to win at 9%, the draw at 15%, and Switzerland to win at 76%. On the Qatar side specifically the market reads 9%, which prices out at American odds of +1063. Compared against the model's 20%, that's the +11.8pp gap the Pick rests on.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Qatar the lower bound is 15%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +6.3pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 22 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: The +11.8pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the Qatar side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the Qatar side still clears the Pick threshold.
copy.summary: A +11.8pp gap across model and market on the Qatar side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Qatar at 20%; Polymarket sits at 9%.
copy.title: Qatar v Switzerland · the model leans Qatar
